title: Former OpenAI Engineer Pleads Not Guilty to Planting Office Bug
summary:
Abdulrahman Alfozan denied felony charges in federal court Friday regarding a surveillance device he is accused of hiding in an executive room at OpenAI. The former employee pleaded not guilty to a count of intercepting oral communications following his Oct. 9 arrest for allegedly bugging a conference room used by the AI lab's leadership.

OpenAI stated there is no evidence its model weights or source code were stolen, and the indictment does not allege the theft of trade secrets or work for a foreign entity. Alfozan has been held in custody since his arrest after a judge determined his ties to Saudi Arabia made him a flight risk. The next hearing is scheduled for Nov. 17.

Former OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan pleaded "not guilty" to bugging an executive conference room at the company.

His lawyer entered the plea Friday, after a grand jury indicted him on a felony count of intercepting oral communications.

He has been jailed since his Oct. 9 arrest after a judge agreed his Saudi ties made him a flight risk.

No charge alleges trade-secret theft or work for a foreign government, and the company reports no sign he took model weights or source code.

So far, the record shows an alleged attempt to overhear an AI lab’s leadership, not what the encrypted recorder caught or for whom.
